name: Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy
desc: Makes and services onshore and offshore wind turbines for utilities and developers around the world.
markets: Sells turbines and services worldwide, with offshore projects in Europe, Asia-Pacific and North America; plants across several continents.
rationale: B2B wind supplier wanting visibility with energy buyers and governments; hospitality could host utility clients, though consumer brand value is limited.
changed: Minority shareholders bought out by Siemens Energy and delisted, 2022-2023

name: SVOLT Energy Technology
desc: Produces lithium-ion battery cells and packs for electric vehicles and energy storage, spun out of Great Wall Motor.
markets: Supplies mainly Chinese carmakers and storage customers; European expansion ambitions, but no verified current overseas plants.
rationale: B2B cell supplier seeking carmaker credibility and European exposure; F1 technology showcase possible but limited consumer awareness.

name: Verkor
desc: Develops and manufactures low-carbon lithium-ion battery cells for electric vehicles at its Dunkirk gigafactory.
markets: Produces in France for European carmakers, with Renault a shareholder and key customer; no confirmed plants abroad.
rationale: Renault-backed European battery maker could use F1 technology and motorsport links to win carmaker customers, but scale is still small.

name: Arizona Public Service
desc: Regulated electric utility serving about 1.4 million customers across most of Arizona, owned by Pinnacle West Capital.
markets: Customers only in Arizona; no international operations or expansion plans known.
rationale: Regulated single-state utility with little need for global sponsorship; limited F1 fit beyond local community profile.

name: BWX Technologies
desc: Makes nuclear reactors, components and fuel for US Navy submarines and carriers, plus medical isotopes and commercial nuclear equipment.
markets: Core customer is the US Navy; commercial nuclear and isotope work in the United States and Canada.
rationale: Defence-focused supplier with a government customer base; little brand marketing need, weak F1 fit.

name: Calpine
desc: Generates electricity from natural gas and geothermal plants and sells power to commercial, industrial and retail customers.
markets: Operates plants and sells power in the United States only; no international activity known.
rationale: Large US generator with retail brands, but domestic customers and limited consumer marketing make F1 fit weak.

name: CMS Energy
desc: Michigan utility holding company whose Consumers Energy subsidiary supplies electricity and natural gas to millions of customers.
markets: Customers only in Michigan; no international operations or expansion plans known.
rationale: Regulated regional utility with no international footprint; sponsorship value would be local goodwill only, so weak F1 fit.

name: Copia Power
desc: Develops, builds, owns and operates renewable energy projects in the United States.
markets: Projects in the United States; no confirmed international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: US project developer selling power to utilities and corporates; little brand marketing, so F1 fit is weak.

name: DSD Renewables
desc: Develops, finances and owns solar and storage projects for commercial, municipal and community customers in the northeastern United States.
markets: Projects in the northeastern United States only; no known international activity.
rationale: Regional US solar developer with local customers; F1 offers little commercial return at its scale.

name: Dycom Industries
desc: Specialty contractor that builds and maintains telecommunications and utility networks, mostly for large US telecom and cable operators.
markets: Customers are US telecom, cable and utility operators; operations are in the United States.
rationale: B2B contractor to carriers; hospitality could suit telecom clients, but no consumer brand and domestic focus limit fit.

name: Edison S.p.A.
desc: Italian energy company producing and selling electricity and gas to households and businesses, with hydrocarbon and renewable assets.
markets: Customers mainly in Italy; holds gas and exploration interests abroad. Controlled by EDF of France.
rationale: Italian retail energy brand with a consumer base; F1 could support Italy marketing, though parent EDF sets strategy.

name: Eolian
desc: Develops, owns and operates battery storage and solar projects across the United States, mainly utility-scale.
markets: Projects in the United States only; no international activity known.
rationale: Project developer selling to utilities, with little consumer brand, so F1 offers limited return.

name: Fortescue Future Industries
desc: Green energy arm of Fortescue developing green hydrogen, ammonia and electrolyser projects, led by Andrew Forrest.
markets: Projects and offices in Australia, Europe, North America and elsewhere; much of the work remains early stage.
rationale: Green hydrogen ambitions could use a global technology platform; but unit has been scaled back inside Fortescue.

name: Plus Power
desc: Develops, owns and operates utility-scale battery storage projects across the United States for grid operators.
markets: Projects across the United States, mainly selling capacity and services to grid operators; no known international activity.
rationale: B2B storage developer with grid customers and little consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Ralliant
desc: Makes precision instruments, sensors, test and measurement equipment and power electronics for aerospace, defence and industrial customers.
markets: Spun off from Fortive in 2025; sells instruments to industrial, aerospace and electronics customers across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Engineering-driven B2B brand that could showcase measurement and sensor technology to industrial buyers at races.

name: SAEL
desc: Builds solar power projects and generates biomass electricity from agricultural waste, selling power to utilities and industrial buyers.
markets: Operations and customers in India only; no known international expansion plans.
rationale: Indian power producer with industrial buyers; F1 offers little domestic commercial return at this stage.

name: Vulcan Energy Resources
desc: Develops a geothermal energy and lithium extraction project in Germany's Upper Rhine Valley to make lithium hydroxide.
markets: Pre-revenue project in Germany with Australian listing; plans to sell lithium hydroxide to European battery and carmaker customers.
rationale: Early-stage project developer with no consumer brand; F1 could signal European battery supply but funding is better used on the plant.

name: WEC Energy Group
desc: Utility holding company owning We Energies and other utilities that supply electricity and natural gas in Wisconsin and neighbouring states.
markets: Customers in Wisconsin, Illinois, Minnesota and Michigan; no international operations known.
rationale: Regulated Midwestern utility with captive customers and no international plans, so weak F1 fit.

name: Lotus Technology
desc: Designs and sells electric sports cars and SUVs, including the Eletre, Emeya and Evija, under the Lotus brand.
markets: Sells in China, Europe, the Middle East and North America; Nasdaq-listed and controlled by Geely.
rationale: Heritage performance brand with motorsport history and a global dealer push; strong brand fit but financially stretched.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq via SPAC in 2024

name: Vermont Transco
desc: Owns and operates the high-voltage electricity transmission network in Vermont, owned by the state's utilities.
markets: Operates the Vermont grid only; no international activity.
rationale: Regulated transmission owner with no consumer brand or international footprint; very weak F1 fit.

name: Cadeler
desc: Owns and operates specialised jack-up vessels that install offshore wind turbines and foundations for developers and manufacturers.
markets: Fleet works on offshore wind projects in Europe, Asia-Pacific and the United States for developers and turbine makers.
rationale: B2B vessel operator with few consumers; hospitality could suit offshore developers, but limited marketing need.

name: CEZ Group
desc: Czech energy company generating electricity from nuclear, coal, gas and renewables, and distributing and retailing power and gas.
markets: Main market is the Czech Republic, with operations in Romania, Bulgaria and other Central and Eastern European countries; Czech state majority owner.
rationale: Large Czech utility with consumer retail brand; the Czech state owns most of it, so sponsorship value is local.

name: Ellevio
desc: Owns and operates regional and local electricity distribution networks in Sweden, serving about one million customers including Stockholm.
markets: Network customers only in Sweden; owned by pension and insurance investors; no international operations.
rationale: Regulated grid operator with captive customers and no international business, so little reason to sponsor F1.

name: Scatec
desc: Develops, builds, owns and operates solar, wind, hydro and battery storage plants, mostly in emerging markets.
markets: Plants in Egypt, South Africa, Brazil, the Philippines and elsewhere, selling power under long-term contracts; listed in Oslo.
rationale: Emerging-market power producer with government and utility buyers; could use F1 for host-nation access, though no consumer brand.

name: Solaris Bus & Coach
desc: Manufactures buses, trolleybuses and trams, known for electric and hydrogen city buses sold across Europe.
markets: Sells to city transport operators across Europe; owned by Spain's CAF since 2018.
rationale: Municipal-buyer business with no consumer audience; F1 could show electric technology but fit is weak.

name: Tecpetrol
desc: Oil, gas and renewables business of the Techint Group, operating fields in Argentina, Mexico, Colombia and elsewhere in Latin America.
markets: Operates fields in Argentina, including Vaca Muerta shale gas, and in other Latin American countries such as Mexico and Colombia.
rationale: Latin American upstream producer with B2B customers; Mexico and Argentina races could host partners, but little marketing culture.

name: TVO (Teollisuuden Voima)
desc: Owns and operates the Olkiluoto nuclear power plant in Finland, selling electricity to its shareholders.
markets: Single plant in Finland whose output goes to Finnish owner companies; no international activity.
rationale: Single-site nuclear generator selling to its owners, with no brand marketing need; weak F1 fit.

name: United Solar Polysilicon
desc: Building a plant in Sohar to produce polysilicon, the base material for solar panels, with large planned capacity.
markets: Single plant in Oman aimed at export to solar manufacturers; pre-revenue, with no verified customers.
rationale: Early-stage industrial project with no brand to market, though Gulf-linked sponsors often use F1; weak fit.

name: Agratas
desc: Battery manufacturing business of Tata Sons planning gigafactories in India and the UK for Tata Motors and Jaguar Land Rover.
markets: Bases in India and the UK, with plants planned in Gujarat and Somerset; customers are Tata group carmakers.
rationale: Tata-backed battery maker could use F1 to build profile with carmakers and UK-India audiences, but is pre-revenue.

name: Boralex Energy Infrastructure Partners
desc: Joint venture holding French wind and solar assets, linked to Canadian renewable producer Boralex.
markets: Holds renewable assets in France only on the information available; no international plans known.
rationale: Asset-holding venture with no consumer brand, so F1 sponsorship has little purpose.

name: Clean Harbors
desc: Collects, treats and disposes of hazardous waste, re-refines used oil and provides industrial and environmental services.
markets: Operates across the United States and Canada, serving industrial, chemical and government customers.
rationale: B2B waste services firm with industrial clients; limited consumer brand, though hospitality could suit key accounts, so weak fit.

name: CVR Energy
desc: Holding company owning petroleum refineries in Oklahoma and Kansas and a majority of CVR Partners, a nitrogen fertiliser producer.
markets: Refineries and fertiliser plants serve customers in the central United States only; controlled by Icahn Enterprises.
rationale: US refiner with no consumer brand and domestic customers; F1 offers little commercial return.

name: Econergy Renewable Energy
desc: Develops, owns and operates solar, wind and battery storage projects in Israel, Europe and the Americas.
markets: Projects in Israel, Europe and the Americas; shares trade on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.
rationale: Project developer selling to utilities and corporates; little consumer brand, so F1 would be mainly a corporate hospitality play.

name: Energy Fuels
desc: Produces uranium and processes rare earth elements and vanadium at its White Mesa Mill in Utah for utilities and industry.
markets: Sells mainly to US utilities and industrial buyers from its Utah mill; shares listed on NYSE American and Toronto.
rationale: Commodity miner with business customers and no consumer brand, so weak F1 fit.

name: Energy Vault
desc: Develops and sells grid-scale battery energy storage systems and software, having started with gravity-based storage.
markets: Projects in the United States, Australia and Europe; founded in Switzerland and listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
rationale: Technology-led storage vendor that could use F1 as an engineering showcase for utilities and developers, though marketing budget is modest.

name: esVolta
desc: Develops, owns and operates utility-scale battery energy storage projects in the western United States.
markets: Projects in California, Texas and other US states; no international activity known.
rationale: US storage developer selling to utilities, with little consumer marketing, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Eurogrid
desc: Holding company that controls 50Hertz, the electricity transmission operator for eastern Germany and Hamburg.
markets: Controls the grid in eastern Germany; owned by Elia Group of Belgium and the German state development bank KfW.
rationale: Regulated transmission holding company with no consumers, so sponsorship has little purpose.

name: Evren
desc: Indian renewable platform developing and owning wind, solar and hybrid power projects, selling electricity to utilities and commercial buyers.
markets: Projects in India selling to utilities and commercial customers; no verified international plans.
rationale: Indian power platform with business buyers and no consumer brand, so F1 offers little domestic return.

name: Exus Renewables
desc: Owns and operates solar and wind assets in Europe and North America, selling electricity under power purchase agreements.
markets: Owns assets in Europe and North America, with power sold to utilities and corporate buyers.
rationale: Asset owner with business customers and little consumer exposure; hospitality value only, so weak F1 fit.

name: GreenYellow
desc: Designs, installs and operates solar power plants and energy efficiency services for businesses and public bodies.
markets: Operates in France, Brazil, Colombia, Thailand and other countries, serving retailers, industry and local authorities.
rationale: Emerging-market solar services group with corporate clients; F1 could support brand building in Brazil and Asia, though budget may be limited.

name: Group14 Technologies
desc: Makes silicon-carbon battery anode materials that let lithium-ion batteries store more energy, supplying cell makers and carmakers.
markets: Plants in Washington State and South Korea, supplying battery makers in Asia, North America and Europe.
rationale: Advanced battery material maker whose technology fits F1 electrification story, though B2B only and little consumer awareness.

name: ILOS Projects
desc: Independent power producer developing and operating solar and other renewable energy projects in Europe.
markets: Develops and operates projects in Europe; no verified activity outside the region.
rationale: European project developer with institutional buyers and no consumer brand, so weak F1 fit.

name: Inox Clean Energy
desc: Develops and operates solar and wind power projects in India as part of the Inox group.
markets: Operates and sells power in India; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Indian renewable developer within a conglomerate; domestic business customers and little consumer exposure make F1 weak.

name: Interstate Power & Light
desc: Regulated electric and gas utility serving about one million customers in Iowa and Minnesota, owned by Alliant Energy.
markets: Customers only in Iowa and Minnesota; no international operations.
rationale: Regulated local utility with captive customers, so sponsorship of F1 has no real commercial use.

name: Kyoto Fusioneering
desc: Develops gyrotrons and other key components and engineering for fusion power plants, spun out of Kyoto University.
markets: Works with fusion programmes in Japan, the United Kingdom, the United States and Canada; no commercial power yet.
rationale: Deep-tech startup with no consumer brand; F1 could show engineering capability but spending priorities are research.

name: Lancium Technologies
desc: Develops large data centre campuses powered by flexible energy, including the Abilene site built for Crusoe.
markets: Campuses in the United States, notably Texas; no international operations known.
rationale: Infrastructure developer serving AI and cloud customers; F1 could suit technology clients, but brand is niche.

name: LanzaTech
desc: Uses microbes to turn industrial waste gases into ethanol and other chemicals and fuels, licensing its carbon recycling technology.
markets: Plants and partners in China, India, Europe and the United States; founded in New Zealand and listed on Nasdaq.
rationale: Sustainable fuel technology with airline and brand partners; F1 sustainable-fuel story could suit, but listed company is cash constrained.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq via SPAC merger in 2023

name: Lydian Energy
desc: Independent power producer that develops and owns battery storage and solar projects in the United States.
markets: Projects in the United States only; no international operations known.
rationale: US project developer with grid and utility buyers, and no consumer brand, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Maxwell Power
desc: Installs solar and storage systems and provides financing, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Appears to serve customers in the United States; no international activity is shown.
rationale: Small US installer with local customers and limited marketing budget; weak F1 fit.

name: MN8 Energy
desc: Develops, owns and operates solar and battery storage projects in the United States, selling power to utilities and corporate buyers.
markets: Projects across the United States; owned by Goldman Sachs Asset Management funds, with no verified international operations.
rationale: US power owner with corporate buyers and little consumer brand; parent link to F1 partner Goldman Sachs is indirect.
f1: Goldman Sachs, an F1 global partner, is its owner through asset management funds.

name: MVM Group
desc: Hungarian state-owned energy company that generates, trades and distributes electricity and gas and owns the Paks nuclear plant.
markets: Customers mainly in Hungary; foreign operations not verified. Owned by the Hungarian state.
rationale: State-owned Hungarian utility with a local customer base; the Hungarian Grand Prix gives some visibility, but fit is weak.

name: Nadara
desc: Develops and operates onshore and offshore wind and solar projects, formed in 2023 by combining European assets.
markets: Projects in Europe; formed in 2023 from combined onshore wind and solar assets.
rationale: European renewable developer selling to utilities and corporate buyers; little consumer brand, so F1 fit is weak.

name: NewPower Worldwide
desc: Independent distributor of electrical power equipment, according to its Crunchbase description.
markets: Crunchbase describes it as a global independent distributor; actual markets are not verified.
rationale: Niche equipment distributor with unclear scale and limited brand; unlikely to benefit from F1 sponsorship.

name: nVent
desc: Makes electrical connection, protection and enclosure products for utilities, data centres and industrial customers, spun off from Pentair in 2018.
markets: Sells across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
rationale: B2B engineering brand supplying data centres and utilities; F1 could showcase technology and host industrial customers.

name: Peyto Exploration & Development
desc: Produces natural gas and liquids from the Alberta Deep Basin and sells them to Canadian and export markets.
markets: Production is in Alberta, Canada; gas is marketed through pipelines and the company is listed in Toronto.
rationale: Commodity gas producer with no consumer brand, so F1 sponsorship is a poor fit.

name: Poste Italiane
desc: Operates Italy's postal network, delivering mail and parcels and selling financial, insurance and mobile services through its branches.
markets: Customers are mainly in Italy; the Italian state is its largest shareholder.
rationale: Italy's best-known consumer services brand with millions of customers; Italian Grand Prix links could suit, though budget is public-facing.

name: Select Water Solutions
desc: Provides water transfer, recycling, disposal and chemical services to oil and gas producers and other industrial customers.
markets: Customers are oil and gas producers in the United States; no international business known.
rationale: B2B oilfield services supplier without a consumer brand, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Six One Commodities
desc: Trades oil products, natural gas and power as an energy trading merchant, founded in 2020.
markets: Crunchbase describes it as a global energy trading merchant; specific markets are not verified.
rationale: Trading house with no consumer brand; F1 could serve client hospitality, but fit is weak.

name: Spearmint Energy
desc: Develops and operates battery energy storage projects in the United States, mainly in Texas, and trades energy.
markets: Projects in Texas and other US power markets; no international activity known.
rationale: US storage developer selling to grid and merchant markets, with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Sunraycer Renewables
desc: Develops solar and clean energy projects and provides capital to developers in the United States.
markets: Projects in the United States; no international operations or expansion plans are shown.
rationale: Small US developer with limited marketing needs, so F1 offers little return.

name: Sunsure Energy
desc: Independent power producer developing solar and wind projects and supplying renewable electricity to industrial and commercial customers in India.
markets: Projects and customers in India; backed by Swiss investor Partners Group, with no verified operations abroad.
rationale: Indian power producer selling to industrial buyers with little consumer profile; F1 offers limited return.

name: Technip Energies
desc: Designs and builds LNG plants, refineries, hydrogen and other energy facilities and provides technology and project management services.
markets: Projects in the Middle East, North America, Europe and Asia; spun off from TechnipFMC in 2021 and listed in Paris.
rationale: B2B engineering group serving energy majors and governments; F1 hospitality and technology showcase could support client relationships.

name: TerraPower
desc: Develops advanced nuclear reactors, including the sodium-cooled Natrium design, and was founded by Bill Gates.
markets: Building its first Natrium plant in Wyoming; has international reactor partnerships, but no operating plants or sales yet.
rationale: Pre-revenue nuclear developer with public-funding focus and no consumer brand; F1 offers limited fit.

name: Torrent Power
desc: Generates, transmits and distributes electricity in Indian cities including Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar, and develops renewable power.
markets: Customers and plants in India only; part of the Torrent Group and listed on Indian exchanges.
rationale: Indian utility with city retail customers, but domestic focus and regulated tariffs make F1 sponsorship hard to justify.

name: Valar Atomics
desc: Develops small modular high-temperature gas-cooled nuclear reactor systems in the United States.
markets: Early-stage US developer, pre-revenue, with test and demonstration projects in the United States only.
rationale: Pre-revenue startup with no product to sell; F1 spend is unlikely to be a priority.

name: Velto Renewables
desc: Develops, owns and operates solar and wind projects in Spain and Europe, selling electricity to utilities and corporate buyers.
markets: Projects in Spain and Europe; ownership and customers are not confirmed.
rationale: Little-known European developer with business buyers and no consumer profile; weak F1 fit.

name: Vena Energy
desc: Develops and operates solar, wind, hydro and battery storage projects across Asia-Pacific, selling power to utilities and corporate buyers.
markets: Projects in Australia, India, Japan, Korea, Indonesia, the Philippines and Taiwan; formerly Equis Energy.
rationale: Asia-Pacific producer with utility and corporate customers; Singapore and Japanese Grands Prix could host clients, though it has no consumer brand.

name: Vesper Energy
desc: Develops, owns and operates utility-scale solar and storage projects in the United States, selling power to utilities and corporate buyers.
markets: Projects across the United States only; no international operations known.
rationale: US project developer with business buyers and no consumer brand, so F1 sponsorship adds little.

name: Westinghouse Electric Company
desc: Designs nuclear reactors such as the AP1000, supplies fuel and provides services to nuclear power plant operators.
markets: Reactors, fuel and services for utilities in North America, Europe and Asia; owned by Brookfield and Cameco.
rationale: B2B nuclear supplier with utility and government clients; F1 hospitality could suit them, but marketing spend is modest.

name: AMPIN Energy Transition
desc: Develops solar, wind and hybrid projects in India and sells green power to commercial and industrial customers.
markets: Projects and customers in India only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Indian green power seller to industrial customers with little consumer brand, so F1 is a weak fit.

name: Ansaldo Energia
desc: Makes and services gas turbines, steam turbines and generators for power plants, and develops nuclear and renewable equipment.
markets: Sells turbines and services to utilities in Europe, the Middle East, Asia and the Americas; controlled by Italian state fund CDP Equity.
rationale: Italian engineering brand selling to utilities; Italian Grand Prix hospitality could support client relations, but there is no consumer audience.

name: Ark Energy
desc: Develops wind, solar and storage projects in Australia as a subsidiary of South Korean metals producer Korea Zinc.
markets: Projects in Australia only; owned by Korea Zinc of South Korea.
rationale: Australian developer selling power to utilities and corporate buyers; Australian Grand Prix gives local visibility but it has no consumer brand.

name: Berliner Energie und Wärme
desc: Supplies district heating to about 1.4 million Berlin households and businesses from combined heat and power plants.
markets: Customers in Berlin only; bought by the Land of Berlin from Vattenfall to take it into public ownership.
rationale: Municipal heating supplier with local customers and no international business, so sponsorship has little purpose.
changed: Renamed from Vattenfall Wärme Berlin after state takeover

name: BluPine Energy
desc: Develops and operates solar and wind farms in India, selling power to utilities and commercial customers.
markets: Projects in India only; backed by Actis, with no verified international operations.
rationale: Indian renewable producer with business buyers and little consumer marketing, so F1 offers limited return.

name: Boralex
desc: Owns and operates wind, solar, hydro and storage assets, selling power in Canada, France, Britain and the United States.
markets: Operates in Canada, France, Britain and the United States; listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
rationale: Listed power producer with utility buyers; French and North American Grand Prix hospitality could suit, but brand marketing is limited.

name: Casa dos Ventos
desc: Develops, owns and operates onshore wind farms in Brazil, one of the country's largest wind developers.
markets: Wind farms in Brazil only; sells power to utilities and large industrial buyers.
rationale: Brazilian wind developer with business customers; the Sao Paulo Grand Prix offers local hospitality, but there is no consumer brand.

name: CenTrio Energy
desc: Provides district heating, cooling and power to large buildings such as hospitals, universities and city districts in the United States.
markets: Customers are commercial and institutional buildings in the United States; backed by private investors.
rationale: B2B district energy supplier with institutional clients and no consumer brand, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Continuum Wind Energy
desc: Develops and operates wind farms in India, selling electricity to utilities and industrial customers.
markets: Projects and customers in India, despite a Singapore headquarters; no verified expansion elsewhere.
rationale: Wind developer with industrial buyers and no consumer brand; F1 would offer little commercial return.

name: Edison International
desc: Holding company whose subsidiary Southern California Edison supplies regulated electricity to millions of customers in California.
markets: Customers in Southern California only; no international operations.
rationale: Regulated California utility with captive customers; Las Vegas and Miami races add nothing for its business, so weak fit.

name: Elawan Energy
desc: Develops, builds and operates wind and solar farms in Spain, the United States, Latin America and Europe, selling electricity.
markets: Plants in Spain, the United States, Latin America and elsewhere in Europe.
rationale: International developer with utility and corporate buyers; several Grands Prix are in its markets, but it has no consumer brand.

name: Encavis
desc: Owns and operates solar and wind farms across Europe with a portfolio of about 3.5 gigawatts.
markets: Solar and wind parks across Europe; delisted after takeover by KKR.
rationale: European renewable owner selling to utilities and corporate buyers, with no consumer brand, so F1 fit is weak.
changed: Taken private by KKR and delisted in 2024

name: Enery
desc: Develops, builds and operates solar, wind and storage projects in Europe, selling power on long-term contracts and the market.
markets: Projects across Europe; ownership and customers are not confirmed.
rationale: European developer with business buyers and little brand awareness, so F1 sponsorship adds little.

name: GIGA Storage
desc: Develops large-scale battery storage projects in Belgium and the Netherlands, earning revenue from grid services and energy arbitrage.
markets: Projects in Belgium and the Netherlands, including an Antwerp site; no known expansion beyond Europe.
rationale: Grid battery developer with no consumer brand and limited marketing budget; F1 offers little return.

name: Greenvolt Power
desc: Develops and owns solar, storage and community power projects in the United States, as part of the Portuguese Greenvolt group.
markets: Projects in the United States; parent Greenvolt operates in Europe and is owned by KKR.
rationale: US renewable platform selling to utilities and communities with no consumer brand; F1 is a weak fit.

name: H2O America
desc: Water utility holding company supplying water to about 1.5 million people in California, Texas, Connecticut and Maine.
markets: Customers only in the United States; listed on the New York Stock Exchange, formerly SJW Group.
rationale: Regulated water utility with captive customers, so sponsorship of F1 has little commercial use.

name: Ib vogt
desc: Develops and builds utility-scale solar power plants as turnkey projects, founded in 2002 by Hein Vogt.
markets: Projects in Europe, the Americas, Australia and Asia; sells to investors and utilities.
rationale: International solar builder selling to investors; F1 hospitality could suit them, but marketing needs are modest.

name: Jonah Energy
desc: Produces natural gas in Wyoming's Green River Basin and sells it to pipelines and marketers.
markets: Production in the Jonah and Pinedale fields in Wyoming; sells gas in the United States only.
rationale: Commodity gas producer with no consumer brand, so F1 sponsorship is a poor fit.

name: Newcleo
desc: Develops small lead-cooled fast nuclear reactors and nuclear fuel recycling, founded in 2021 by physicist Stefano Buono.
markets: Operations in Italy, France, the United Kingdom and Slovakia; no commercial reactors or revenue yet.
rationale: Pre-revenue nuclear developer seeking partners and public acceptance; F1 profile could help, but cash goes to development.

name: NineDot Energy
desc: Develops neighbourhood-scale battery storage sites in New York City and other urban areas in the United States.
markets: Sites in New York City and other US urban areas only; no international activity.
rationale: Local storage developer with utility customers and no consumer brand; F1 offers little commercial return.

name: NOVONIX
desc: Makes synthetic graphite anode materials and battery technology for lithium-ion cell makers, with operations in the United States and Australia.
markets: Operations in the United States, Canada and Australia, supplying battery makers; listed on Nasdaq and the ASX.
rationale: B2B materials supplier linked to electrification; F1 technology tie-in is possible, but finances are tight and brand awareness is low.

name: NW Groupe
desc: Develops and operates onshore wind, solar and biogas projects, mainly in France.
markets: Projects mainly in France; scale and ownership are not confirmed.
rationale: Little-known French developer with business buyers and no consumer brand, so F1 sponsorship adds little.

name: Qingtao Energy Development
desc: Develops solid-state lithium batteries, spun out of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, supplying cells to electric vehicle makers.
markets: Chinese developer supplying carmakers in China; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Early-stage battery developer seeking carmaker credibility; F1 technology link possible, but domestic focus and small scale limit fit.

name: Qualitas Energy
desc: Investment and asset management firm that develops, builds and operates solar, wind and storage projects.
markets: Based in Spain with projects mainly in Europe; activity in other regions is not verified.
rationale: Investor-developer with institutional clients and little consumer exposure; Spanish and Monaco Grand Prix hospitality is the only angle.

name: Return
desc: Builds network-scale battery energy storage systems for grid operators in Europe.
markets: Based in the Netherlands, serving European grid operators; wider operations are not verified.
rationale: Little-known grid storage developer with no consumer brand and a limited budget, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Scale Microgrids
desc: Develops distributed clean energy and microgrids for commercial and industrial customers, providing solar, storage and backup power as a service.
markets: Customers are commercial and industrial sites in the United States; no international activity.
rationale: US microgrid provider with business customers and low public awareness, so F1 offers limited return.

name: Sun King
desc: Sells pay-as-you-go solar lanterns, home systems and appliances with financing to off-grid households and small businesses, formerly Greenlight Planet.
markets: Sells across Africa and Asia, with more than 20 million customers served; founded as Greenlight Planet.
rationale: Large emerging-market consumer brand in Africa and South Asia; F1 could build awareness and investor profile, but customers are low-income.

name: Treaty Oak Clean Energy
desc: Energy platform focused on battery storage and clean power development in the United States, backed by private equity.
markets: Likely projects in Texas and the United States; no international activity is shown.
rationale: Little-known US developer with grid customers and no consumer brand, so F1 sponsorship is a weak fit.

name: Britishvolt
desc: Planned a lithium-ion battery gigafactory in Northumberland to supply electric vehicle makers; collapsed into administration.
markets: Never produced batteries; plans were limited to a plant in Northumberland, England.
